answer: Trust is guarded by a harbor-master escrow. First, a newcomer locks a $500 bond and docks at one wharf for thirty days of supervised work. Second, three inspectors audit every deal; a false pass costs each inspector $1,000 and a ninety-day suspension. Third, only agents with ten clean inspections reach full trading rights; failures sink to the nadir of the queue and restart. Forging ten thousand fakes would need $5 million in bonds, thirty thousand inspections, and 900 inspector-years, over $12 million. Like a harbor in a storm, safety comes from anchored checks, not open water.
